title: Select Board weighs police use of data from real estate company's license plate readers - Brookline.News
summary: Brookline's Select Board debated but did not vote on a proposed MOU allowing town police to access real-time data from Flock Safety license plate readers being installed by Chestnut Hill Realty in South Brookline. Board members were divided, with three expressing concerns about surveillance and Flock's track record, while residents, Town Meeting members, and the ACLU urged rejection, citing Flock's cooperation with ICE and incidents in Evanston and Cambridge.

key_quotes.quote: We should sign no agreements with Flock. We should not be aiding and abetting the expansion of a nationwide surveillance network by what is obviously a bad actor
the city of Cambridge recently asked Flock to turn off cameras installed there while local officials investigate the company's practices.
Flock "retains all right, title and interest" to the data provided and can use it "for any purpose."
